newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat bids judged aggressive, max $161/t.
newsitem.headline: French wheat bids judged aggressive, max $161/t.

text.p: Bids for wheat through France at today's European Union tender were "very aggressive," according to grain exporters, who said the best bid of 8.73 Ecus in subsidy meant a world price of around $161 per tonne, fob April.
First indications of bidding details were that the European Commission would be able to drop refunds to around 9.5 Ecus per tonne to keep up a volume of 300,000 tonnes, traders said.

The toughest bid of 8.73 Ecus accounted for some 125,000 tonnes of wheat, they said. "This is very aggressive," said one exporter, who accused one firm of trying to "break the market" at the expense of others in need of licences to cover sales.
Volume was high at 1,097,500 tonnes, but traders noted there would be a break in tenders next Thursday for Easter.
French cereals office ONIC said earlier the range of bids for refunds was between 8.73 Ecus, giving the highest world price, and 17.99 Ecus per tonne.

Traders gave the following partial cumulative breakdown of wheat bids through France by refund cut-off level: 125,000 tonnes at 8.73 Ecus, 195,000 tonnes at 9.0 Ecus, 330,000 tonnes at 9.5 Ecus, 465,000 tonnes at 10.0 Ecus, 529,000 tonnes at 10.5 Ecus and 677,000 tonnes at 11.0 Ecus.
"That's the one," predicted one expert of the 9.50 Ecu level, noting this would keep EU wheat around two dollars over U.S. soft red winter with a French price of $160 per tonne.

But others said it was difficult to predict what the Commission would decide, with the market still split between a handful of long position holders and a still sizeable, if dwindling, band of companies with uncovered short-term needs.
With no meeting next week, refunds awarded now will carry an extra 1.1 Ecu increment for April compared with those awarded during April itself so near-term pressure for refunds is high.
Last week the EU awarded 273,500 tonnes of soft wheat export licences at a maximum rebate of 11.47 Ecus per tonne.
Benchmark U.S. soft red winter is seen around $158 per tonne for April. The one-month dollar/franc has eased to 5.64 francs this week from 5.73 a week ago.
